qt: to the Commission Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Diana Iovanovici Şoşoacă (NI), Geadis Geadi (ECR), Thomas Geisel (NI) Subject:

The EU calls on citizens to consume less, recycle more and make sustainable choices. Yet when software updates end or essential apps stop working, consumers are compelled to discard devices that function perfectly well. The result is higher costs for consumers, more raw materials and a mounting electronic waste crisis. The world generated 62 million tonnes of electronic waste in 2022, up 82 % since 2010. Only 22.3 % of the waste was officially recorded as having been collected and recycled. The European Parliament has taken steps to extend the lifespan of devices and software support, but how far do these measures protect consumers from having to replace phones and computers whose hardware still works? 1.

Has the Commission assessed the number of perfectly functional hardware devices discarded due to software updates ending or essential apps no longer working and the resulting costs for consumers and the environment? If so, what were the findings of this assessment?
When will the Commission publish its proposed new ecodesign rules for computers, and will these require software support that allows people to use their computers for longer?
How will the Commission prevent the withdrawal of software support from unnecessarily shortening the useful life of phones and computers?
